findings.title: Session-range matching compares dates as strings
findings.description: `_label` tests `request.start <= day < request.end` on strings built with `str(row["range_start"])` and `str(session["session_date"])`. This is only correct if both sides are always zero-padded ISO `YYYY-MM-DD`. If `debug requests` ever renders a datetime (`2026-11-01T00:00:00+00:00`), the comparison silently mislabels sessions. A mislabel can hide an unaccounted session behind "acquisition failed", or fail a session that is accounted for. The same string-key fragility applies to `RequestKey` in `resubmit_origins` and `_check_scope`, where `req["start"]` must match `str(row["range_start"])` exactly. A mismatch there fails safe, with "no recorded original". Parse to `date` and compare dates, or assert the format at the boundary.

findings.title: Duplicated open-ended-want check
findings.description: `latest_want_end` and `cutover_304_evidence.coverage_reads` both loop over `TICK_UNIVERSE` histories and raise the same "want has no end date" `CutoverError`. This is the logic duplication the project's DRY rule forbids. Put one iterator of bounded history wants in a shared module. Both functions can then consume it.

findings.title: Tests depend on private helpers and exact message text
findings.description: The tests call `accounting_futures._product_payload` and `tick_debug_cmds._cell`, which are private. They also assert on message fragments such as `"--estimate run prints"`. Using the real CLI shapes is the right idea, because it keeps the parser tests honest. But a rename of either private helper will break the tests with no behavior change. Consider exposing a public serializer, or adding one contract test that pins these shapes.

findings.title: Scripts named for slice 304 now serve every purchase slice
findings.description: The `cutover_304_*` module names, `prog="cutover_304_first_purchase.py"` and the `PASS_*` constants now describe a shared tool. The docstring explains this, but the names mislead. Renaming is optional and can wait for a later cleanup.

findings.title: `__doc__` is read without a None guard
findings.description: `__doc__.split("\n")[0]` raises `AttributeError` under `python -OO`. This is minor for an operator script.

findings.title: Explicit failure behavior and exception handling
findings.description: Missing keys, an unmapped product, an unparseable timestamp, an unknown session bucket, a failing `gh` call and an unreadable dataset edge all raise `CutoverError` with distinct messages. No silent defaults were introduced. The `SystemExit` catch in `main` is at the process boundary and has a justifying comment. The new modules stay under about 300 lines. The tests cover each stop condition and the boundary cases: an edge equal to the minimum, and a session one position before the publication tail.
